title: Pacemaker check
what: The doctor places a special wand over the device and reads its data. The battery and leads are checked, and settings are changed if needed.
why: Regularly after implant: usually after a few months, then every 6 to 12 months. Your doctor will set the timing.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; results right away
tell_doctor: Any fainting, dizziness, shortness of breath, or strong heartbeat
If your medicines changed since the last check

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: None needed. Eat and take your medicines as usual.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that lets you uncover the device area easily.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Your pacemaker card is a must.

bring: Your discharge papers from the implant
steps: ECG stickers are placed on your arms and legs
The programmer wand is placed over the device on your chest
The doctor reads the data and checks how it works
Sometimes settings are changed. Your heart may beat differently for a short time
The doctor explains the result and sets the next check
feel: Sometimes your pulse changes or you feel dizzy for a few seconds. Tell the doctor
after: Write down the date of the next check
Carry your device card with you
red_flags: Fainting or severe dizziness: call emergency services
Your pulse becomes very slow or very fast
Redness, swelling, or discharge over the device

faq.q: How long does the battery last?
faq.a: Usually many years. The check shows how much is left, and your doctor will tell you in advance when to replace it.

faq.q: Can the device be checked remotely?
faq.a: Some devices allow it. Ask your doctor if yours does.

reminders.text: Pacemaker check tomorrow. Bring your device card and medicine list.
